# `Browser.Vibration`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Browser.Vibration — drive the device vibration actuator over `Ipe.Ffi.Js`
ports.

A first-party proof of the per-capability web mechanism spanning BOTH port
directions: outbound `JsCmd`s (`vibrate` / `pattern` / `cancel`) request an
actuator operation, and an inbound `JsMsg` carries the acknowledgement or a
typed unavailability. Both cross the same seal codec and fail-closed port
discipline as every other port; there is no second transport.

Importing this reserved `Ipe.Browser.<Api>` module discloses `js-port:vibration`
(import-derived, keyed on the canonical `Ipe.Browser.Vibration` path prefix via
`WebCapability::for_browser_module`, alias-immune); only the top-level app's
`[capabilities] accepts` set can grant it.

The two layers:

  * `Ipe.Browser.Vibration.Internals` publishes the closed outbound/inbound ADTs
    and the raw `Ipe.Ffi.Js` wiring.
  * this module is the high-level layer: `vibrate` / `pattern` / `cancel` are
    `Cmd`-shaped (fire-and-forget), and `acknowledgements` is the inbound
    subscription folding the narrow `JsMsg` into a typed `Result Error ()`. The
    inbound `case` is EXHAUSTIVE: an unavailability becomes a typed `Err`, never
    a silently dropped variant.

## `vibrate`

```ipe
vibrate : Int -> Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`vibrate ms` — vibrate for `ms` milliseconds. Outbound `Cmd`; an absent
actuator traps to a typed inbound result on the `acknowledgements` subscription,
never a panic.

Importing this module discloses `js-port:vibration`; the app must grant it with
`accepts = [ JsPort Vibration ]` under [capabilities] in package.ipe.

## `pattern`

```ipe
pattern : List Int -> Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`pattern durations` — vibrate/pause along the alternating on/off `durations`
(each in milliseconds). Outbound `Cmd`.

## `cancel`

```ipe
cancel : Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`cancel` — stop any ongoing vibration. Outbound `Cmd`.

## `acknowledgements`

```ipe
acknowledgements : (Result Error () -> msg) -> Sub.Sub msg
```

`acknowledgements toMsg` — the inbound subscription, wired in `subscriptions`.

The decoder IS the security gate: every inbound value runs through the total,
bounded seal decoder for the narrow `JsMsg`; a malformed / mismatched frame is
dropped whole. A decoded `JsMsg` is folded EXHAUSTIVELY into a
`Result Error ()` — a `Vibrated` becomes `Ok`, an unavailability a typed `Err`.
